q: Adiabatic quantum computation (AQC) and its relation to the circuit model: Aharonov-van Dam-Kempe-Landau-Lloyd-Regev (2007) showed that AQC and the quantum circuit model are:
opts: AQC is strictly weaker (cannot solve all BQP problems)
Polynomially equivalent — each can simulate the other with at most polynomial overhead
AQC is strictly stronger (solves NP-complete problems efficiently)
AQC is equivalent to classical computation
exp: ADKLLR theorem: AQC and BQP are polynomially equivalent. Any quantum circuit can be simulated by adiabatic evolution (with spectral gap Ω(1/poly(n))), and any AQC can be simulated by a quantum circuit. This means AQC is a universal quantum computing model.
